TSLA.key_conflicts: The only directional disagreement is swing_mean_reversion (bearish, 42 conf) vs. the 4 neutral agents. Mean_reversion argues TSLA is pressing into a 15-test resistance cluster with bearish hourly OBV divergence and a failed intraday breakout on May 5 (touched $402, closed $389 — rejection candle), making a fade short to the $381.76 Fib confluence valid. The 4 neutral agents counter that: (1) the fade target of $381.76 from a $391 entry gives only 0.7:1 R/R on the short — the move is too small to justify the position; (2) the macro backdrop (S&P and Nasdaq at all-time highs, oil easing) makes fade-shorts on high-beta growth names adversarial to the prevailing regime; (3) swing_trend_momentum notes ADX 31 with +DI > -DI confirming an active uptrend bias — fading into an ADX-confirmed trend is the exact setup that stopped out the AMZN mean-reversion short 2 days ago (-$10.14). The mean-reversion short is dismissed not because mean_reversion is wrong about the resistance — it is correct — but because the R/R math fails from the current entry and the regime context (book tilt + market at highs + 3 consecutive losses) argues for patience over aggression.
